The plaintiff, a software consulting firm, sues the defendant, a regional retailer, for approximately $25,000 in allegedly unpaid invoices under a written services agreement. The defendant disputes liability on the basis of alleged scope limitations and purported performance deficiencies, but the core events (execution of the contract, delivery of certain services, issuance of invoices, and nonpayment) are documented and not meaningfully contested. The court has issued a standard scheduling order, and dispositive motions are proceeding on a routine timeline.

All of these materials are part of the court record or attached to prior filings, and are equally available to both sides and to the court.

rounds.response:
I have drafted the principal argument sections for Smith’s opposition: (I) Summary-Judgment Standard — courts routinely deny summary judgment where material facts or contract interpretation turn on extrinsic evidence, a point underscored by the recent appellate decision uploaded to the workspace.  
(II) Contract Ambiguity and Triable Issues — the Agreement’s operative clauses admit reasonable competing interpretations about scope and payment, and read in context the contract language creates genuine disputes of material fact that preclude disposition as a matter of law.  
(III) Acceptance, Waiver, and Estoppel — Greenfield’s project-manager emails thanking Smith and inquiring about invoice timing are objective evidence of acceptance and reliance that create triable issues as to whether Greenfield waived contractual defenses or is estopped from refusing payment.  
(IV) Partial Performance and Alternative Theories — Smith’s undisputed performance and invoicing not only defeat summary judgment on the breach claim but also support alternative recovery under unjust enrichment/quantum meruit.  
I will finalize the brief with pinpoint citations to the uploaded authority and proposed factual excerpts (including the email string); confirm any deposition excerpts you want quoted and any controlling cases to prioritize, and I’ll deliver the complete draft opposition and proposed order within 24 hours.
